p_note: ONS Census 2021, Southampton local authority 248,900 (0.92 x); p stands
note: Centre Southampton; covers Eastleigh, Winchester, the New Forest, Bournemouth, Poole, Salisbury, Andover and Weymouth with Portland; airport SOU. Portland is reached only through Weymouth, so the whole isle goes with Weymouth rather than Exeter.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Sheffield local authority 556,500; p 685,368 is the 2011 built-up area and stands (0.81 x)
note: Centre Sheffield; covers Rotherham, Barnsley, Doncaster, Chesterfield and Worksop; Doncaster Sheffield airport has closed, so the nearest are Manchester and East Midlands. The Peak District bounds it on the west; Leeds lies north of Barnsley.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Portsmouth local authority 208,100 (1.07 x); p stands
note: Centre Portsmouth on Portsea Island; covers Gosport, Fareham, Havant, Waterlooville, Chichester and Bognor Regis. The Southampton edge runs between Titchfield and Fareham; the South Downs separate it from London to the north.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Peterborough local authority 215,700 (1.32 x); under 1.5 x, p stands
note: Centre Peterborough; covers the Fens: Spalding, Boston, Wisbech and King's Lynn, with the Wash coast. Flat open farmland; edges against Cambridge, Nottingham and Leicester are drawn round villages only.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Oxford local authority 162,100; p matches
note: Centre Oxford; covers Abingdon, Didcot, Witney, Bicester, Newbury and Swindon. London takes the Chilterns and Thames valley east of Thame and Goring; Bristol takes Wiltshire west of Swindon; Birmingham and Northampton meet it south of Banbury.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Nottingham local authority 323,632; p 729,977 is the 2011 built-up area, the area meant, and stands
note: Centre Nottingham; covers Derby, Mansfield, Loughborough, Newark, Grantham and Lincoln; East Midlands airport (EMA). A narrow wedge reaches west to Kingsley between Sheffield and Birmingham; it is old and left as it is.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Norwich local authority about 144,000; p 143,135 matches
note: Centre Norwich; covers Norfolk: Great Yarmouth, Lowestoft, Thetford and the north Norfolk coast; airport NWI. Reach to 89 km over open farmland to the Wash side, where King's Lynn falls to Peterborough.

p_note: Northampton 245,899 is the built-up area figure; ONS 2021 West Northamptonshire is larger but covers a county area. p stands
note: Centre Northampton; covers Milton Keynes with Bletchley, Woburn Sands and Cranfield, Bedford, Kettering, Wellingborough, Rushden and Daventry; no airport of its own (Luton and Birmingham). The London edge sweeps south of Bletchley and Bedford; the M1 corridor ties it together.

p_note: ONS 2011 built-up areas via Wikipedia: Tyneside 774,891 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyneside) plus Wearside (Sunderland built-up area) 335,415 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wearside); proposed p = 1,110,306 after the Sunderland merge
note: Centre the Grey Street core between Central Station and the Quayside; covers Tyneside and Wearside (Gateshead, South Shields, Sunderland, Washington), Durham, Chester-le-Street, Peterlee and Northumberland to the Scottish border; airport NCL. The Teesside edge runs between Durham and Spennymoor and along Castle Eden Dene south of Peterlee.

p_note: ONS 2011 Teesside built-up area 376,633 via Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teesside); no 2021 Teesside figure, the 2021 list splits it
note: Centre Middlesbrough town centre; covers Teesside (Stockton-on-Tees, Redcar, Billingham, Hartlepool), Darlington, Spennymoor, Bishop Auckland, Weardale and Teesdale, Northallerton, Thirsk, Wensleydale, Helmsley and the moors coast to Whitby; airport MME. Scarborough and Pickering stay with Hull; Ripon, Masham and Easingwold with Leeds.

Centre Charing Cross; hand-painted to reach past 100 km along the commuter rail lines: Reading, Slough, High Wycombe, Luton, Watford, Basildon, Southend and Crawley; airports Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted, Luton, City. Edge refinement only round villages on its rim.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Leicester local authority 368,600; p matches
note: Centre Leicester; small outline taking Wigston, Oadby, Market Harborough and Corby; nearest airport East Midlands. Loughborough sits with Nottingham and Hinckley and Coalville with Birmingham, so Leicester's extent is tight; a candidate for Colin to widen.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Leeds local authority 811,956 (Leeds City Council); 1.78 x the old p of 455,123, which was the core. GeoNames 536,280 is the 2021 built-up area. Proposed p = 811,956
note: Centre Leeds; covers West Yorkshire (Bradford, Huddersfield, Wakefield, Halifax, Dewsbury), York and Harrogate; airport LBA. The Pennines bound it on the west against Manchester; the Sheffield edge runs along the Barnsley-Wakefield line. The north edge with Middlesbrough runs south of Hawes, Bedale and Thirsk, keeping Masham, Ripon and Easingwold.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Kingston upon Hull local authority 267,014 (0.85 x); p stands
note: Centre Hull; covers both shores of the Humber (Grimsby, Cleethorpes, Scunthorpe via the Humber Bridge), Beverley, Bridlington and Scarborough; Humberside airport. The Humber estuary is crossed by the bridge, so the south bank belongs here.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Ipswich local authority 139,700 (0.78 x); p 178,835 is the built-up area and stands
note: Centre Ipswich; covers Felixstowe, Colchester, Clacton-on-Sea and Bury St Edmunds. London takes Essex south of Marks Tey; Norwich the land north of the Waveney valley.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Cambridge local authority 145,700; p matches
note: Centre Cambridge; covers St Neots, Haverhill, Ely, Newmarket and, down the M11 corridor, Great Chesterford and Saffron Walden; airport STN is London's. London takes the line north of Newport and Royston; the Fens go to Peterborough; Norwich holds the Breckland edge.

p_note: Hand-painted city with a customised name; p 617,353 covers the Brighton-Worthing coastal belt, not the local authority (277,103, ONS 2021). Left for Colin
note: Centre Brighton; hand-painted to cover the Sussex coast from Littlehampton and Worthing to Eastbourne, Bexhill and Hastings, with Burgess Hill; airport Gatwick sits in London. Edge refinement only: the London line was moved round Burgess Hill and two villages.

p_note: ONS Census 2021, Birmingham local authority 1,144,919 (1.16 x p); the West Midlands conurbation is larger. Under 1.5 x, so p stands
note: Centre Birmingham; covers the West Midlands conurbation (Wolverhampton, Dudley, Walsall, Solihull), Coventry, Telford, Worcester, Shrewsbury, Stafford and Banbury; airport BHX. Open Midlands land: edges are drawn round towns against Manchester (Stoke-on-Trent), Bristol (Cheltenham), Leicester, Nottingham, Oxford and Northampton.
